findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit log datetime key
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but this implementation inherits the numeric `Paginator` key logic and calls `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)`. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` reaches cursor construction and raises `TypeError` instead of returning a page. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible `get_item_key` and cursor conversion, or the endpoint must continue using `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Changing live buffer keys from sets to sorted sets has no compatibility path
findings.body: This now issues `ZADD` against the existing `span-buf:s:*` key names, while deployed versions stored those keys as Redis sets. During a rolling deploy, or for up to the existing one-hour TTL after deployment, any trace with an already-buffered set causes Redis `WRONGTYPE` here; the corresponding pipeline/batch fails and spans are not processed. The Lua script has the same incompatibility via `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`. Use versioned keys or explicitly migrate/handle legacy set keys before reading or writing them.

findings.title: Reduced redirect traversal limit can split deep traces into separate segments
findings.body: Redirect mappings are not rewritten for every descendant when a partial tree is merged, so resolving an old descendant can require walking the parent chain. Lowering the bound from 10,000 to 1,000 means traces deeper than this are resolved to an intermediate buffer rather than the actual segment root. Subsequent spans are then stored and flushed as a different segment, losing the intended trace assembly. Retain the prior bound or introduce path compression/a safe mechanism that preserves correctness for deep trees.
